lines.text: Do you know how an escalator works? It's one long loop of steps, going round and round.
A motor at the top pulls a chain, and the steps ride along it. Up the front, and back down underneath.
Each step has two sets of wheels on two tracks. Where the tracks spread apart, the step stands up into a stair. Where they come together, it folds flat.
The handrail is its own loop, driven to move at the same speed as the steps.
At the end, a comb plate slides between the grooves, so nothing gets pulled under.
In eighteen ninety six, an early moving stairway at Coney Island was so new, people rode it just for fun.
